title: L-S Coupling (Russell-Saunders Coupling)
short_intro: L-S coupling is a quantum mechanical scheme in multi-electron atoms where individual orbital angular momenta (l<sub>i</sub>) couple together to form a resultant total orbital angular momentum (L), and individual spin angular momenta (s<sub>i</sub>) couple to form a resultant total spin angular momentum (S). These resultant vectors then interact via spin-orbit coupling to yield the total angular momentum (J).

exam_scope.tgt_core: Basic understanding of quantum numbers n, l, m<sub>l</sub>, m<sub>s</sub>, vector atom model representation, and total angular momentum quantum number J in multi-electron systems.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Detailed derivation of vector addition for L-S coupling, determination of term symbols (<sup>2S+1</sup>L<sub>J</sub>), Hund's rules for ground state determination, and application to multi-electron atomic spectra.

prerequisites: Bohr's theory of hydrogen atom and spatial quantization

concept_notes.heading: Physical Origin of L-S Coupling
bullets: Valid primarily for light and medium-weight atoms where electrostatic Coulomb repulsion between electrons is much stronger than the magnetic spin-orbit interaction.
Individual orbital angular momenta (l<sub>i</sub>) of all electrons vector-add to form a total orbital angular momentum vector L.
Individual spin angular momenta (s<sub>i</sub>) of all electrons vector-add to form a total spin angular momentum vector S.

concept_notes.heading: Formation of Total Angular Momentum J
bullets: The resultant orbital vector L and resultant spin vector S interact via spin-orbit interaction to form the total angular momentum vector J.
Mathematically expressed as J = L + S.
The magnitude of total angular momentum is given by |J| = \sqrt{J(J+1)}\hbar, where J can take values ranging from |L - S| to L + S in integer steps.

concept_notes.heading: Russell-Saunders Term Symbols
bullets: State of an atom in L-S coupling is represented by the spectroscopic term symbol <sup>2S+1</sup>L<sub>J</sub>.
2S+1 represents the spin multiplicity of the state.
L is denoted by letters S, P, D, F, G... corresponding to total orbital quantum numbers L = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4...

concept_notes.heading: Hund's Rules for Ground State Determination
bullets: Rule 1: For a given electron configuration, the term with the maximum multiplicity (2S+1) lies lowest in energy.
Rule 2: For a given multiplicity, the term with the largest value of total orbital angular momentum L lies lowest in energy.

Rule 3: For shells less than half-filled, the level with the minimum J value (J = |L - S|) has the lowest energy; for shells more than half-filled, the level with the maximum J value (J = L + S) has the lowest energy.

derivations.title: Magnitude of Total Angular Momentum in L-S Coupling
derivations.conditions: Assuming vectors L and S precess rapidly about their resultant J due to spin-orbit interaction.
steps: Write the vector sum relation for total angular momentum: J = L + S.
Take the dot product of J with itself: J^2 = (L + S)\cdot(L + S) = L^2 + S^2 + 2(L\cdot S).
Substitute quantum mechanical operator eigenvalues: J(J+1)\hbar^2 = L(L+1)\hbar^2 + S(S+1)\hbar^2 + 2(L\cdot S).

derivations.title: Spin-Orbit Interaction Energy Shift in L-S Coupling
derivations.conditions: First-order perturbation theory applied to spin-orbit interaction energy E<sub>so</sub>.
steps: The spin-orbit Hamiltonian is given by H<sub>so</sub> = \zeta_{LS}(L\cdot S), where \zeta_{LS} is the spin-orbit coupling constant.
Evaluate the dot product L\cdot S using L^2, S^2, and J^2 operator relations: L\cdot S = \frac{1}{2}[J(J+1) - L(L+1) - S(S+1)]\hbar^2.
Substitute into the energy shift equation: \Delta E_{so} = \frac{1}{2}\zeta_{LS}[J(J+1) - L(L+1) - S(S+1)]\hbar^2.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Vector Model of L-S Coupling
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Vectors L and S precessing rapidly around their resultant vector J, while J itself precesses slowly around an external axis (or in space).
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Illustrates conservation of angular momentum components and the hierarchical coupling strength where L and S couple first before interacting with J.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Frequently asked in conceptual multiple-choice questions regarding vector orientations and precession cones.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Stern-Gerlach Experiment (Spatial Quantization)
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A beam of silver atoms passing through an inhomogeneous magnetic field splitting into two distinct traces on a detector plate.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Proves space quantization of angular momentum and existence of electron spin (s = 1/2, giving 2s+1 = 2 components).
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Directly tested as foundational background for understanding vector atom models and angular momentum coupling.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Multiplet Splitting Energy Level Diagram
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: Energy levels of a term symbol splitting into multiple J-levels under spin-orbit interaction (e.g., <sup>2</sup>P splitting into <sup>2</sup>P<sub>1/2</sub> and <sup>2</sup>P<sub>3/2</sub>).
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: Demonstrates the Landé interval rule where the separation between adjacent J levels is proportional to the larger J value.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Used in numerical and theoretical questions regarding fine structure splitting in atomic spectra.

solved_numericals.question: Find the possible values of total angular momentum quantum number J for an atomic state with L = 2 and S = 1.
solution_steps: Use the rule for possible J values: J ranges from |L - S| to L + S in integer steps.

solved_numericals.question: Determine the ground state term symbol for an atom with configuration np<sup>2</sup> using Hund's rules.
solution_steps: For np<sup>2</sup>, two p-electrons have n = np, l = 1, s<sub>1</sub> = 1/2, s<sub>2</sub> = 1/2.
Possible m<sub>l</sub> values are 1, 0, -1. Applying Pauli's exclusion principle, maximum total spin S = \sum s_i = 1, giving multiplicity 2S+1 = 3 (Triplet).
Maximum total orbital angular momentum L compatible with Pauli exclusion is L = 1 (P state).
For a shell less than half-filled (np<sup>2</sup> has 2 electrons out of 6), the lowest J value is J = |L - S| = |1 - 1| = 0.

solved_numericals.question: Calculate the Landé g-factor for the state <sup>2</sup>P<sub>3/2</sub>.
solution_steps: Identify quantum numbers from <sup>2</sup>P<sub>3/2</sub>: Multiplicity 2S+1 = 2 \implies S = 1/2. Letter P \implies L = 1. Subscript J = 3/2.
Write the Landé g-factor formula: g = 1 + \frac{J(J+1) + S(S+1) - L(L+1)}{2J(J+1)}.

assumptions_and_limitations: L-S coupling assumes electrostatic repulsion between electrons is much stronger than magnetic spin-orbit interaction, which fails for very heavy elements where j-j coupling dominates.

common_misconceptions.wrong: L-S coupling means individual electron spins couple directly to individual orbital angular momenta of other electrons.
common_misconceptions.correct: Individual orbital momenta couple to form L, and individual spins couple to form S; L and S then couple together.
common_misconceptions.why: Russell-Saunders coupling assumes intra-atomic electrostatic forces group all l<sub>i</sub> together and all s<sub>i</sub> together before spin-orbit interaction takes place.

common_misconceptions.wrong: The term symbol <sup>2S+1</sup>L<sub>J</sub> has J as the principal quantum number.
common_misconceptions.correct: J represents the total angular momentum quantum number of the atom.
common_misconceptions.why: J is the vector sum of L and S, completely distinct from the principal quantum number n.

quick_revision: In L-S coupling, L = \sum l_i, S = \sum s_i, and J = L + S with magnitude J ranging from |L - S| to L + S.
